Project-specific extension for the Quranic figure Dhul-Qarnayn.
    In Islamic tradition widely identified with Alexander / Iskandar.
    Covers the prophetic and righteous-ruler aspects (building the wall against Gog and Magog, 
    seeking the Water of Life, etc.) that are not fully captured by the classical Iconclass notation.

Project-specific extension for the birth of the Prophet Muhammad. 
    The mother reclines on a couch while the newborn is handed to one of two attending angels. 
    The composition is known from Ilkhanid manuscript painting (notably the Edinburgh 
    Jāmiʿ al-Tawārīkh) and later prophetic cycles. 
    No exact official Iconclass notation exists for this Islamic prophetic subject; 
    the term is therefore marked as limited-scope.

    bringing forth (or leading) the she-camel of God (nāqat Allāh) from the side of a

    notation. The visual formula is well-attested in Jāmiʿ al-Tawārīkh and Qiṣaṣ al-Anbiyāʾ 
    manuscripts.

comment.value:
Project-specific extension for the scene in which Moses (Musa), 
    standing or seated on a rock/mountain and often wearing a prophetic veil, 
    hears the voice of God emerging from the clouds, while the seventy elders 
    (or learned men) lie prostrate below him. 
    Mountains form the background. 
    This composition is particularly characteristic of Ilkhanid manuscript painting 
    (notably the Edinburgh Jāmiʿ al-Tawārīkh) and reflects both Biblical 
    (Exodus 24; Numbers 11) and Islamic narrative traditions.

    (Sūrat al-Kahf 18:9–26). Emphasises the Islamic narrative details: the 309-year sleep, 
    the dog (Qiṭmīr), and the alternative location of the cave in Toyug (Central Asia) 
    rather than Ephesus. Used when the painting or text clearly follows the Islamic tradition.

nodes.label: Moses and the seventy elders hearing the voice of God from the clouds

attrs.comment:
Project-specific extension for the scene in which Moses (Musa), 
    standing or seated on a rock/mountain and often wearing a prophetic veil, 
    hears the voice of God emerging from the clouds, while the seventy elders 
    (or learned men) lie prostrate below him. 
    Mountains form the background. 
    This composition is particularly characteristic of Ilkhanid manuscript painting 
    (notably the Edinburgh Jāmiʿ al-Tawārīkh) and reflects both Biblical 
    (Exodus 24; Numbers 11) and Islamic narrative traditions.

Project-specific extension covering the Quranic prophet Shuaib 
    (identified with or related to Jethro). 
    Captures the distinctive themes of preaching to Midian, 
    fair weights and measures, and the destruction of the people of Midian/Aykah.

Project-specific extension for the birth of the Prophet Muhammad. 
    The mother reclines on a couch while the newborn is handed to one of two attending angels. 
    The composition is known from Ilkhanid manuscript painting (notably the Edinburgh

    No exact official Iconclass notation exists for this Islamic prophetic subject; 
    the term is therefore marked as limited-scope.

Project-specific extension for the Qur’anic version of the Seven Sleepers 
    (Sūrat al-Kahf 18:9–26). Emphasises the Islamic narrative details: the 309-year sleep, 
    the dog (Qiṭmīr), and the alternative location of the cave in Toyug (Central Asia) 
    rather than Ephesus. Used when the painting or text clearly follows the Islamic tradition.

rows.sourceLabel: Moses and the seventy elders hearing the voice of God from the clouds
rows.targetLabel: the book Exodus: story of Moses and Aaron
rows.comment:
Project-specific extension for the scene in which Moses (Musa), 
    standing or seated on a rock/mountain and often wearing a prophetic veil, 
    hears the voice of God emerging from the clouds, while the seventy elders 
    (or learned men) lie prostrate below him. 
    Mountains form the background. 
    This composition is particularly characteristic of Ilkhanid manuscript painting 
    (notably the Edinburgh Jāmiʿ al-Tawārīkh) and reflects both Biblical 
    (Exodus 24; Numbers 11) and Islamic narrative traditions.

rows.targetLabel: the book Exodus: story of Moses and Aaron
rows.comment:
Project-specific extension covering the Quranic prophet Shuaib 
    (identified with or related to Jethro). 
    Captures the distinctive themes of preaching to Midian, 
    fair weights and measures, and the destruction of the people of Midian/Aykah.

rows.comment:
Official Iconclass notation for the discovery of the infant Moses 
    floating in a basket on the Nile by Pharaoh’s daughter and her maidens. 
    In Persian and Islamic manuscript painting the scene often shows Queen Bithia 
    (with long dark hair) and an Israelite nurse of lighter complexion.

Jonah (Yunus) reclining in the shade of the gourd plant (or vine) 
    that God caused to grow to shelter him after he was cast up by the great fish 
    (Jonah 4:6). 
    The reclining pose is continuous with early Christian iconography. 
    In Persian and Islamic manuscripts the sea creature is frequently shown as a large fish.
